handoff.factLogAction: On the old disk. Everything it had already published is safe in the cloud; anything still in its outbox is not. If the old disk is readable, copy store.sqlite across before starting the new server.
handoff.factsTitle: What survives the machine, and what does not
handoff.intro: Every file a store server needs, regenerated for {store}. Use this when the machine has died, is being replaced, or was never set up from the wizard.
handoff.keyHint: Optional: a box activated with a code syncs without one. A key is scoped to this store, with read_config and relay_orders — the two the store sync routes need. Issuing one does not disable the old key; revoke that separately once the new box is up.
handoff.keyIssued: Key issued. It is now baked into the files below and will not be shown again.
handoff.linuxHint: Run as root with the binary and the unit file. Same layout: update slots, both files below, the systemd unit, the port on a running ufw or firewalld, then the service.
handoff.secretWarning: Three of these four files contain the store's key. Treat them as passwords and delete them once the new box is up.
handoff.step1: Copy the binary and the installer across, and run the installer.
handoff.step2: Read the boot log and look for "pos_edge listening".
handoff.step3: Issue an activation code on the Activation screen, open the box's address on any device on the shop LAN, and type the code on /setup.
handoff.step4: Pair the tills: the installer prints the pairing URL, and the log holds it too.
handoff.step5: Take the old machine off the network, and revoke its key. Two boxes on one store both sell today — the lease supersedes the old one for updates, not for trading.
handoff.title: Move this store to another machine
handoff.windowsHint: Run in an elevated PowerShell with the binary. Lays out the update slots, writes the config, opens the listen port on the Private firewall profile, registers the service with its failure actions, and starts it.
handoff.withoutKey: The files below carry no key. The new machine syncs with the credential it gets when an activation code is typed on its /setup screen.

settings.item.backup.interval_hours.help: How many hours apart the store sends a sealed backup of its database off the store box. It is the most trading the store can lose if the box's disk dies. A change applies from the next backup. No value switches backups off.
settings.item.counter.walk_in_channel.he: Whether an order the counter starts for a walk-in guest is taken away, eaten in, or asked each time. The channel decides the order's prices and its tax. Takeaway is as before. With Ask, the counter shows Eat in and Take away when an order is started. Where the store limits the channels it accepts, it must accept this one, or the counter's orders are refused.
settings.item.locale.tax_rounding.help: How each tax amount and each fee rounds to the smallest unit of the store's currency: the tax of each tax class, whether prices include it or not, the tax on a fee, and the fee itself. Round half up rounds half a unit or more up, as before. Round down drops the fraction. The total still rounds to the store's cash rounding as before, and a dish's price does not change. A bill is worked out with the rounding in force at the time, so change it while the store is closed.
settings.item.locale.tax_rounding.title: Tax rounding
settings.item.permissions.enforced.help: Turning this on decides every act at the till with the signed-in person's own permissions, and refuses what their roles do not grant. Check that each role holds what its staff need before you turn it on.
settings.item.permissions.enforced.title: Each person's own permissions
settings.item.printing.font_size_dots.he: How large the store server draws a line its printers cannot print in their own characters, such as a Vietnamese dish name, in printer dots: 24 is a comfortable receipt body. A line in the printer's own characters keeps the printer's font. Double-size text is drawn twice as large. A change applies from the next print.
The language a receipt, its copy and a pre-bill print their labels and dish names in. A dish the menu does not translate keeps its own name. Until the store's country is set, or where receipts have no labels in its language, the country's language prints as the display language.
settings.item.printing.receipt_printed_o: Whether taking a payment prints the guest's receipt. Off, the till's print button prints a copy.
settings.item.printing.receipt_second_la: A second language for a receipt, its copy and a pre-bill. Each label prints in both, side by side, or the second under the first where the paper is too narrow. A dish, a modifier or a fee the menu or its fee rule translates prints its name in the second language under its own. None prints one language, as before.
settings.item.printing.receipt_tax_compo: Whether a receipt, its copy and a pre-bill print each tax line's breakdown under its rate, such as CGST and SGST in India, wherever the Tax rates screen breaks a rate down. Off, each prints the tax line alone, and every sale still records the breakdown. A copy prints the breakdown its sale recorded. A store whose rates have no breakdown prints the same either way.
settings.item.qr.table_order.help: Whether a guest's QR order joins the order a table already has open, so the table has one order and one bill, or stays an order of its own on the table. Where staff confirm guest orders, it joins once they confirm it. A table whose bill is already open or paid keeps the guest's order separate. A dish that joins keeps the price the guest saw, and is taxed as the table's order is.
settings.item.qr.table_order.title: A guest's QR order at a table with an open order
A security setting: how long a till may sit with no touch before it signs its person out and locks, until their PIN opens it again on the screen they left. 0 never locks. The kitchen board and the pass never lock.
settings.item.session.lockout_attempts.h: A security setting: how many wrong PINs in a row lock a person out, counted across sign-in and a manager's approval together. No value switches the lockout off.
settings.item.session.lockout_minutes.he: A security setting: how long a person stays locked out after too many wrong PINs. No value switches the lockout off.
settings.item.session.pin_min_length.hel: A security setting: the fewest digits a staff PIN may have, for every store. It applies when a PIN is set or reset. A PIN already set keeps working, so reset a person's PIN to hold them to a new minimum. A policy choice: a PIN's defence is its hashing and the lockout.
settings.item.session.pin_min_length.tit: Fewest digits in a staff PIN
settings.item.session.sign_in_idle_timeo: A security setting: how long a signed-in till may go unused before it asks for a PIN again. It also bounds how long a till carried off while signed in keeps working.
settings.item.shift.blind_close.help: Whether the count at the close of a shift is blind. On, the till says nothing about what the drawer should hold until the shift closes, so the cashier counts first. Off, the Shift screen shows the cash the drawer should hold beside the count.
settings.item.shift.blind_close.title: Blind count at close
settings.item.shift.close_report.help: What prints when a drawer's shift closes: each drawer's report where it is closed, one slip for several drawers closed together, or nothing. The close still shows the drawer's figures on the till.
settings.item.shift.close_report.title: Report at a drawer's close
settings.item.shift.drawer_day_end.help: What happens to a drawer whose shift is still open once its business day has ended: flag it on the till and in the console, or also refuse cash, paid in and paid out into it until it is counted and closed. Cards, the count, the close and opening the drawer without a sale still work.
settings.item.shift.drawer_day_end.title: A drawer left open past its day
settings.item.shift.drawer_model.help: Whether the store keeps one cash drawer for every till, or a drawer for each till, started, counted and closed on its own. A change waits until no drawer is open. With a drawer for each till, cash is taken only at a device bound to a till, and each till's drawer opens at the receipt printer its terminal names. Before switching, bind each device to its till on the till's Devices screen, and mark each terminal's receipt printer as having a cash drawer.
settings.item.shift.drawer_model.title: Cash drawers
settings.item.shift.no_shift_selling.hel: Whether a till may seat a table, start a counter order or take a payment while no shift is open.
The float the Shift screen fills in when a shift opens, in the smallest unit of the store's currency: 500000 is 500,000 đồng. The cashier can change it before opening the shift. 0 fills in nothing.
settings.item.shift.variance_reason_mino: How far over or short a drawer may close, either way, before its close asks a reason, in the smallest unit of the store's currency: 50000 is 50,000 đồng. The till asks only after the count, so the count stays blind. 0 asks no reason, as before.
Reason for a large over or short
settings.item.tender_keys.first_tip_perc: The first tip key on the pay screen, as a whole percentage of the bill: 10 is 10%. 0 hides the key. The till shows the keys in this order, after No tip, wherever the store takes tips.
settings.item.tender_keys.second_tip_per: The second tip key on the pay screen, as a whole percentage of the bill. 0 hides the key, and so does the first key's percentage.
settings.item.tender_keys.split_ways_max: The most guests the pay screen offers to split a bill between evenly, from 2 to 12: it offers every number from 2 up to this one. Above 6, the row of numbers scrolls sideways on a narrow screen.
Most guests in an even split
settings.item.tender_keys.third_tip_perc: The third tip key on the pay screen, as a whole percentage of the bill. 0 hides the key, and so does an earlier key's percentage. With no key left, the pay screen shows no tip row.

settings.presetsNone: This store already sets every setting that has a new-store value.

settings.readOnly: Your role can read these settings but not change them, because every change publishes to stores.
settings.refused.archived: That store group is archived, so a value set for it would reach no store.
settings.refused.notFound: That brand, store group or store no longer exists. Reload the page and choose again.
settings.refused.nothingThere: Nothing is set here any more. The page now shows what is.
settings.refused.unknownSetting: This cloud has no such setting. Reload the page.
settings.refused.value: This setting does not take that value.
settings.republishHint: For a store whose last settings publish failed, or that has moved to another brand or store group since.
settings.runs.group: {store} runs “{value}”, set for the store group {name}.
settings.scopeHint: A store runs the value of the most specific level that sets one: the store itself, then its store groups, then its brand, then every store. Where none sets one, it runs the default.
settings.storeUnknown: {store} has not reported which release it runs, so it may not honour this yet. It is honoured from release {since}.
settings.switchShowsDefault: Not set here: the switch shows the default.
settings.switchShowsRuns: Not set for this store itself: the switch shows what it runs.

settings.value.DRAWER_DAY_END_REQUIRE_CL: Refuse cash until it is closed
settings.value.NO_SHIFT_SELLING_REFUSE: Refuse until a shift is open
settings.value.RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_COUNTRY: The language of the store's country
settings.value.TABLE_ORDER_SEPARATE: Keep it an order of its own
settings.varianceReasonUncovered: The reason list offers no reason for closing a drawer over or short, so this limit asks nothing and every drawer closes as before. Add one valid for "Close a drawer over or short" on the Reason codes screen, and publish it.
setupFile.hint: The release's own pos-edge.exe, named for this store and this cloud. Double-click it on the shop's PC: it asks for administrator rights, installs the service, and opens the activation screen. No script, and nothing to type.
setupFile.needsHttps: This console is open over plain http, and a setup file tells the store to dial the cloud over https — the only way a store dials it. Open the console at its https address to download one.
setupFile.noKey: The setup window asks for a store key; press Enter to skip. The machine syncs with the credential its activation code gives it, so it does not need one.
setupFile.notHosted: This cloud does not hold release {release} for Windows. Put it in the cloud from the OTA screen first.
setupFile.pasteKey: When the setup window asks for the store key, paste the key shown above. It goes only into the service's own registry key.
setupFile.releaseHint: The version to install — the one your stores run, on the OTA screen. The box updates itself from there.
setupFile.title: Windows setup file (.exe)
setupFile.unsigned: If the release is not code-signed, the browser or Windows may warn about the file. When the browser asks, keep the file. When Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, choose More info, then Run anyway. It happens once per PC; later updates install without asking.
stations.archiveStationMessage: The station stops receiving fired items and any rule pointing to it is dropped on the next publish. You can restore it later.
stations.defaultHint: Items with no matching rule are routed here. Set this on exactly one station.
stations.description: A store's kitchen stations and the rules that route a fired item to one. Each station can name a backup for printer failover and say when its tickets are late and which language they print in, and one station can be the catch-all default. Publish after changing stations or routing.
stations.lateAfterHint: How long a ticket waits before this station's kitchen display marks it late: a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60. Leave it empty for 10 minutes.
stations.lateAfterInvalid: Late after must be a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60, or empty for 10 minutes.
stations.loadHint: Load to see this store's kitchen stations.
stations.name: Station name
stations.needItemAndStation: Choose both a station and an item.
stations.needStationFirst: Add a station first — a rule routes to one.
stations.publishHint: Publishing compiles this store's kitchen stations and routing — together with its areas and tables — into the plan the store applies. Publish after changing stations or routing.
stations.removeRuleMessage: Items this rule matched will fall back to the default station until you add another rule.
stations.routingEmpty: No routing rules yet — items go to the default station.
stations.routingHint: A rule sends a fired item to a station. An item with no rule goes to the catch-all default station.
stations.sortInvalid: Order must be a whole number.
stations.stale: Someone else changed this station while you were editing. The list has been reloaded — please check and try again.
stations.ticketLanguageHint: The language this station's kitchen tickets print in: their labels, and each dish's name where the menu translates it. A ticket that goes to a backup station's printer prints in the backup's language. The kitchen display keeps its own language.
stations.title: Kitchen stations
storeGroups.authoredHint: Nothing more to choose: this is recompiled from what you have already authored, and every shop in the group gets the result.
storeGroups.caution.qr: Check the time-zone offset before publishing this to a cohort that spans more than one. It is a value you typed, not one taken from each shop's own settings, so the same offset will be published to every shop in the group.
storeGroups.caution.tender: An empty list of payment methods means a shop takes no payment at all. Published to a group, that stops settlement at every shop in it.
storeGroups.copyFromHint: This setting is typed per shop, so the group takes a copy of one shop's current value. Set it on that shop first, then publish it to the rest.
storeGroups.description: Publish one change to a whole cohort of shops instead of one shop at a time.
storeGroups.emptyHint: Create one and add the shops that take the same menu, the same tax registration, or the same change first.
storeGroups.historyHint: What this group has been sent, newest first. A shop whose last outcome was not “Published” is not running what the rest of its group runs.
storeGroups.listHint: A group is a set of shops you publish to as one. It is not the brand: a shop belongs to one brand and to as many groups as you need — the airport branches, the shops on one tax registration, the pilots that take a change first.
storeGroups.membersHint: The whole membership, not a change to it — what you save here is what the group holds. A group may hold up to 200 shops.
storeGroups.menuPrerequisite: A shop with no tax rates or no locale settings yet is skipped rather than published to — it would take the order and then fail at the payment screen.
storeGroups.name: Name
storeGroups.nameHint: Name it after what the shops in it have in common, because that is what you will look for when you publish.
storeGroups.noBatches: Nothing has been published to this group yet.
storeGroups.nodeHint: A store's country, timezone and legal identity are not here: those are per-shop by definition, so they stay on the shop's own settings screen.
storeGroups.pickASource: Choose a shop to copy from
storeGroups.publishHint: This runs the same publish once per shop in the group. It is not all-or-nothing: every shop gets an outcome, and a shop that was skipped or refused is named below with the reason.
storeGroups.sourceHasNoNode: That shop has not published this setting yet, so there is nothing to copy.
storeGroups.stale: Somebody else changed this group while you were editing it. Its current state is shown; apply your change again.
storeGroups.title: Store groups
storeSettings.badTimezone: Not a timezone this browser knows
storeSettings.cashNotesHint: The notes a guest hands over, comma-separated, smallest first — 10000, 20000, 50000. Blank offers the exact amount only.
storeSettings.cashRoundingHint: What the total rounds to when settling in cash — 1000 for Vietnam, 100 for India's rupee. Blank means no rounding.
storeSettings.countryHint: Which country this store is in. Required — a hosted store's region is compared against it, and the fleet console cannot answer “where is this store's data?” without it.
storeSettings.countryRequired: Choose the country this store trades in before publishing.
storeSettings.cutoffHint: 0–23. Before this hour, the trading day is still the previous calendar day.
storeSettings.description: The store's currency, timezone, and business-date cutoff. Publishing sends them to the store, which bills in this currency and rolls its trading day over at the cutoff.
storeSettings.filledFrom: Filled in from {country}. Change anything this store does differently before publishing.
storeSettings.fromCountryHint: Fills in the currency, language, quoting posture, rounding and notes from that country's pack. Every field stays editable.
storeSettings.identityHint: What the receipt says about who sold. A Japanese qualified invoice and an Indian tax invoice are not valid without the seller's name and registration number; every field is omitted from the paper when it is blank.
storeSettings.retentionHint: How long the store PC keeps the record of every sale once the cloud has it. Nothing the cloud has not received is ever deleted, and neither is anything an open order, bill or shift still needs; this is the floor, not a deadline. The cloud can be rebuilt from the stores within this window.
storeSettings.languageHint: The locale the store shows item names in. Blank shows each item's default name.
storeSettings.linesHint: One line per printed line. Blank lines are dropped.
storeSettings.nothingPublished: Nothing published for this store yet — the framework's defaults are shown. Publishing sends exactly what is on this form.
storeSettings.pricesIncludeTaxHint: Tick where the menu price is what the guest pays — Japan's 税込 and India's MRP. Unticked adds tax on top, which is how Vietnam quotes.
storeSettings.registrationHint: Checked for the shape the country issues, never for whether it is registered — that is a call to the tax authority, and a till must not need one.
storeSettings.runningNow: Showing what this store is running now.
storeSettings.runningNowAt: Showing what this store is running now — published {when}.
storeSettings.tillMoneyRejected: Some of what you typed is not a positive whole number and will not be published. Rounding and notes are amounts in minor units.
storeSettings.title: Store settings
storeSettings.tradingNameHint: The sign over the door, when it differs from the registered name. The receipt leads with this.
stores.archiveMessage: Archive this store? It stops appearing in active lists but is not deleted, and can be restored later.
stores.brandArchiveMessage: The brand stays in the registry and stops being offered for new stores. Stores already assigned to it keep their link.
stores.description: Name, create, and organise this tenant's stores and brands — no ULID needed.
stores.empty: No stores yet. Create one below.
stores.name: Name
stores.stale: Someone else changed this store while you were editing. The list has been reloaded — please check and try again.
stores.tenantArchiveMessage: This is the organisation you are working in. Archiving it does not delete anything, but it marks the whole org closed — switch context afterwards.
stores.title: Stores & brands
subjects.description: Look up, export, or erase one data subject's personal data by id — to fulfil a PDPD/GDPR access, portability, or erasure request. Per-subject and audited; owner-only.
subjects.eraseConfirmPrompt: Type the subject id to confirm
subjects.eraseMessage: This masks every personal field permanently, keeping only the id so records still reconcile. It cannot be undone. Confirm the erasure request is valid first.
subjects.guardrail: Confirm the lawful basis and the subject's identity before processing. Confirm consent and retention; for customer analytics, a DPIA. Escalate an EU-resident rights request to the Data Protection contact — this tool records who acted, it does not replace their review.
subjects.notFound: No subject with that id belongs to this tenant.
subjects.ownerOnly: Subject requests are owner-only. Ask an owner to action this request.
subjects.title: Subject requests
taxRates.blankHint: A blank cell means the class is not sold on that channel — the store refuses such a sale rather than charging no tax. Rates are in percent.
taxRates.breakdownHint: A breakdown prints the rate as named lines on the invoice — type CGST 2.5, SGST 2.5. India needs it; leave it blank to print one line.
taxRates.breakdownMalformed: Type each part as a name then a percent, separated by commas.
taxRates.breakdownNeedsRate: Give the cell a rate before breaking it down.
taxRates.breakdownUnbalanced: The parts do not add up to this cell's rate.
taxRates.description: The rate each tax class charges on each sales channel. Edit the grid, save, then publish to a store — the store bills these rates.
taxRates.noClassesHint: Create tax classes on the Menu screen first; each becomes a row here.
taxRates.publishNeedsStore: Choose a store in the top bar to publish.
taxRates.stale: Someone else saved these tax rates while you were editing. The grid has been reloaded — please check what changed and try again.
taxRates.title: Tax rates
translations.description: The tenant's message catalogue. English is required for every key and is the fallback for the rest.
translations.empty: No translations yet. Add a key below.
translations.importSummary: {created} to create, {updated} to update, {rejected} rejected. Nothing is written until you apply.
translations.missingEn: Every key needs a non-empty English value.
translations.missingOnly: Show only keys with a missing translation
translations.stale: Someone else saved this translation grid while you were editing. The grid has been reloaded — please check what changed and try again.
translations.title: Translations
webhooks.deleteMessage: This permanently removes the endpoint and stops all delivery to it. This cannot be undone.
webhooks.deleteTypePrompt: Type the endpoint URL to confirm
webhooks.description: HTTPS endpoints that follow a store's event log. The destination is vetted before it is stored.
webhooks.secretOnce: Copy this signing secret now — it is shown only once.
webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.urlHint: Deliveries follow the store you are working in.
wizard.bindPortHint: Leave blank to use the default 8787. Set it only when something else on the box already holds that port — it is a property of this machine, not of the store, so it never reaches the cloud.
wizard.configHint: Save this as config.toml on the store server, beside the pos_edge binary (or point POS_EDGE_CONFIG at it). It names which store this box is and which cloud to dial. It carries no secret — that is the env file below.
wizard.description: Set up a store from zero — details, an optional API key, and the next steps. No ULID needed.
wizard.doneHint: Two steps remain before this store can trade. Both links below open scoped to the store you just created.
wizard.envHint: The store's one secret. Install it as root, mode 0600, at /etc/pos-edge/env — the service unit reads it from there. Keep it out of config.toml and out of version control.
wizard.envNoKey: No key was issued, so this file has no credential. Go back and issue one, or paste an existing key into the file before installing it.
wizard.installerHint: A single script that lays the box out correctly: it creates the service user and the update-slot layout, writes both files above, installs the systemd unit, then starts the service. Run it as root with the binary and the unit file: sudo sh install-pos-edge.sh ./pos-edge ./pos-edge.service. Running it twice is safe.
wizard.installerSecret: This script contains the store's key. Treat it as a password, and delete it once the box is up.
wizard.installerWindowsHint: The same handoff for a Windows till: it lays out the update slots, writes the config with an absolute database path, registers the service, sets the store key in the service's own registry key rather than machine-wide, and sets the failure actions that bring the box back after an update. Run it in an elevated PowerShell with the binary: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install-pos-edge.ps1 -Binary .\pos-edge.exe. Running it twice is safe.
wizard.keyIssued: API key issued — copy it now, it will not be shown again.
wizard.nextConfig: Set up and publish this store's settings
wizard.nextDrawers: This store keeps a drawer for each till. Before it takes cash, give each terminal its receipt printer with its cash drawer marked, under Devices, and bind each till to its terminal on the till's Devices screen.
wizard.presetsApplied: {count, plural, =0 {This store needed no new-store settings.} one {Gave this store the new-store setting: {list}.} other {Gave this store the new-store settings: {list}.}}
wizard.presetsApplying: Giving the store the new-store settings…
wizard.presetsFailed: The store is created, but its new-store settings could not be applied: {reason}
wizard.presetsRetry: Open Shared settings for this store
wizard.presetsUnpublished: The new-store settings are saved, but they could not be published to the store yet. Publish the store again from Shared settings.
wizard.publishOrder: Publish in this order: Store settings, then Tax rates, then the Menu, then People. A menu published before its tax rates reaches a store that cannot close a bill.
wizard.skipKey: Skip the key — go to the setup files
wizard.skipKeyHint: The store's machine syncs with the credential its activation code gives it, so it can sell and sync without a key.
wizard.step1Hint: Name the store and, optionally, put it under a brand.
wizard.step2Hint: Optional. A store key lets a box you set up by hand reach the cloud; a machine activated with a code syncs without one. The key is shown once.
wizard.title: New store
